title: Secretary of State of Rhode Island

context.text: Secretary of State Gregg Amore is the only candidate on the November 3 ballot for this office.

candidates.name: Gregg Amore
candidates.ballotNote: Incumbent; the only candidate for this office on the general-election ballot.
candidates.currentRole: Rhode Island Secretary of State (since January 2021)

priorities.text: Rhode Island Civic Leadership Program for high school students, which he says has drawn over 300 participants from more than 50 schools, and more than 120 voting and civics lessons.
An improved state archives building and history center, according to Rhode Island Current's report of his campaign launch.

record.text: Declined in 2025 to give the U.S. Department of Justice confidential voter-registration data (driver's license and Social Security numbers), offering the publicly available voter list instead; the Justice Department sued him on December 2, 2025.
U.S. District Judge Mary McElroy dismissed the Justice Department's suit in April 2026; the department appealed on June 4, 2026, and the case is pending before the 1st U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals.

Received a Sept. 4, 2026 Justice Department letter directing him to preserve records from the 2024 election, which said he is “under investigation and ongoing litigation” over compliance with federal election laws; his office had not responded as of Sept. 16, per Rhode Island Current.

sources.title: Flanked by labor and Democratic leaders, RI Secretary of State Gregg Amore kicks off reelection bid
DOJ hits Rhode Island with lawsuit over voter list data
DOJ orders Amore to preserve 2024 election records in ongoing voter data fight

researchNotes: The official certified candidate list for the general election could not be loaded (the Rhode Island Secretary of State and Board of Elections candidate pages returned 403/404); the single-candidate slate rests on Rhode Island Current's voter guide and Ballotpedia, which agree. Records come from news coverage because sos.ri.gov was not reachable. No positions on the fixed issue statements were found; Amore's views on voter ID or citizenship proof were not located.
